PSALM 76

. On Neginoth--(See on , title). This Psalm commemorates what the preceding anticipates: God's deliverance of His people by a signal interposition of power against their enemies. The occasion was probably the events narrated in ; Is 37:1-28. (Compare ).
1-2. These well-known terms denote God's people and Church and His intimate and glorious relations to them.

3. brake ... the arrows--literally, "thunderbolts" (), from their rapid flight or ignition (compare ; ).

the battle--for arms ().

4. Thou--God.

mountains of prey--great victorious nations, as Assyria (Is 41:15; , ; ).

5. slept their sleep--died ().

none ... found ... hands--are powerless.
6. chariot and horse--for those fighting on them (compare ).
7. may ... sight--contend with Thee (; ).
8-9. God's judgment on the wicked is His people's deliverance (; ).

10. Man's wrath praises God by its futility before His power.

restrain--or, "gird"; that is, Thyself, as with a sword, with which to destroy, or as an ornament to Thy praise.
11-12. Invite homage to such a God (), who can stop the breath of kings and princes when He wills ().
